title: Emotional and Financial Support in Schools for Students with Divorced Parents
what_it_is: Emotional and Financial Support in Schools for Students with Divorced Parents

sections.label: School support for students
sections.summary: Schools check in with students after parents' marital status changes and provide counselling, welfare and financial support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: When the school is informed of a change in parents’ marital status by either the parents or the students, the teachers will check in with the students and assess their needs to decide what support is appropriate and necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For students who exhibit emotional distress or social and behavioural changes, or where there is a need for counselling support, School Counsellors and Student Welfare Officers in school will provide individual counselling or group programmes for the students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Students who require financial support can apply for the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) to meet essential school expenditure such as school and miscellaneous fees, textbooks and school uniforms, and transport and meal subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: While updates on marital information is based on voluntary disclosure by parents to schools, the teachers will look out for any changes in the behaviour of their students and follow up with these students and their parents when there is a cause for concern.

sections.label: Children of divorced parents doing well
sections.summary: The speaker says studying children of divorced parents who do well is important, as many have done well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: On the study of children of divorced parents who are doing well, I think it is very important for us to do that because if you look at the outcome of the recent study, whilst it is indicative that there could be some less favourable responses or outcomes of children of divorced parents, there are significant number of children of divorced parents who have done well, too.

sections.label: Studying children with positive outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker encourages MSF and MOE to study children with positive outcomes and the factors behind their success.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: And amongst us, I am very sure we all know that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: I would encourage MSF to work together with MOE to venture into studying deeper with reference to children with positive outcomes and to look at factors that have made it possible for these children to have succeeded.

sections.label: School leaders see Primary school challenges
sections.summary: MOE allows school leaders, but not all teachers, to have sight of Primary school children who faced challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: What MOE has done now is to allow school leaders to have sight of some of these Primary school children who may have had some challenges while they were in Primary school, but not all teachers.

sections.label: Alerting school personnel early
sections.summary: If a child shows early challenges, school leaders can alert School Counsellors, Student Welfare Officers and some teachers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Should the child show some indication of challenges early, the school leaders would then be able to alert the school personnel, like the School Counsellors and the Student Welfare Officers, as well as some of his teachers, to be able to help the child.
